results.summary: Problem 5 (Lanczos) was already cleaned (test0 starting vector de-palindromized to avoid breakdown). All three frozen targets are exactly reproduced by the standard three-term Lanczos recurrence with q1 = b/||b|| and beta = ||v|| >= 0. The only load-bearing convention not stated in the solver-visible text is that the input vector b is the (normalized) starting Krylov vector, i.e. Q[:,0] = b/||b||. results.verify_detail:
CONFIRMED. The 13.11/13.12 cross-step CONTRADICTION trap is real.

WHAT THE 13.12 TEST DOES (verbatim, eval_clean/data/problems_test.jsonl):
  maxwell = Maxwell(50,2)
  x,y,z = np.meshgrid(...)
  fields = (x,y,z,x,y,z, z*0+1)
  stepper(maxwell, fields, courant, t_const)   # return value DISCARDED
  assert np.allclose(check_constraint(maxwell), target)
check_constraint(maxwell) reads maxwell.E_x/E_y/E_z (per its docstring). The Maxwell constructor (13.6, gold-faithful) initializes E_x=E_y=E_z=zeros((n,n,n)). The test never assigns maxwell.E_x before stepper; `fields` is only a local tuple. So the ONLY path to nonzero E inside the object is stepper mutating maxwell.E_* in place.

SOLVER-VISIBLE TEXT FOR 13.11 (stepper) DESCRIBES PURELY FUNCTIONAL BEHAVIOR:
- docstring: "Returns the updated simulation time and the updated fields after the integration."
- return_line: `return time, fields`
- 13.10 update_fields likewise returns `new_fields` functionally.
- The 13.11 target itself is the tuple (time=0.2, [7 fields]); the 13.11 test consumes the return value via cmp_tuple_or_list(stepper(...), target) and does NOT inspect maxwell.E_x. So a solver can fully pass 13.11 with a stepper that never writes to the maxwell object. Nothing in 13.10/13.11/13.12 solver-visible text instructs in-place mutation of maxwell.E_*.

MY FAITHFUL ATTEMPT (tmp/p13_faithful.py, all 15 steps written from solver-visible text only; stepper implemented the NATURAL functional way matching the docstring/return_line, no mutation of maxwell):
  test 0: our value = 0.0, target = 3.976748296795863  -> FAIL
  test 1: our value = 0.0, target = 3.6465516824464292 -> FAIL

results.verify_detail:
Both claimed HIGH UNIT_TRAPs (27.2 and 27.3) are REFUTED. The cm^-3->m^-3 conversion the trap calls an unrecoverable hidden convention is in fact forced by elementary dimensional analysis, because the constants ARE explicitly pinned in SI in the solver-visible step text: "The vacuum permittivity is 8.854e-12 F/m and the electron charge is 1.6e-19 C" (27.2 step_description_prompt).

Faithful implementation (solver-visible text only):
- 27.1 Fermi: phi_p=0.0259*ln(N_A/n_i), phi_n=0.0259*ln(N_D/n_i) (kT=0.0259 V given). No unit issue (log of a ratio). PASSES.
- 27.2 capacitance: from step_background, C = eps*A / sqrt(xi^2 + (2*eps/q)*(phi_b - V0)*((N_A+N_D)/(N_A*N_D))), eps=es*eps0, phi_b=phi_p+phi_n.
- 27.3 get_3dB_frequency: C=capacitance(...); f_3dB = 1/(2*pi*R*C) (step_background). Broadcasts over array xi automatically.

Why the conversion is the MOST NATURAL reading, not a trap: with eps0 in F/m, the term (2*eps/q) has units 1/(V*m); times (phi_b-V0) [V] gives 1/m; the doping factor (N_A+N_D)/(N_A*N_D) has units 1/concentration. For that second term to equal m^2 (matching xi^2), concentration MUST be m^-3. So a competent expert who converts xi (um->m) and A (um^2->m^2) to match F/m -- a step the trap ITSELF concedes is required and natural -- is compelled by the identical dimensional-consistency argument to convert N cm^-3 -> m^-3 (x1e6). It is not an extra, ungrounded convention; it is the same SI-consistency step applied to the third quantity.
